answer: A proof-of-storage protocol deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to prove local custody of unique data sectors. Candidate nodes must commit drive capacity to hold raw archival shards—such as relic telemetry, shale spectroscopy, or saffron crop logs—and solve periodic challenge audits. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of purchasing dedicated disk space per identity. However, this requirement penalizes lightweight edge agents and incurs persistent input-output latency.
